stories.title: Florida inches up FPI, sit just outside top 25 after beating Kentucky
stories.summary: The Florida Gators' Week 11 upset win over the Kentucky Wildcats moved them up the Football Power Index rankings to just outside the top 25. The FPI measures team strength and is meant to be the best predictor of a team's performance for the rest of the season; it shows how many points above or below average a team is. Each team is assigned a rating that measures its true strength on a net-points scale, as well as its expected point margin against an average opponent on a neutral field. Projected results are based on 20,000 season simulations using FPI and the schedule. Take a look at how Florida's numbers shake out after Week 11's upset victory.

stories.title: New observations challenge evidence for an 'outsize' black hole in the early universe
stories.summary: A recent reanalysis of the outsize black hole galaxy UHZ1 using existing X-ray data and new infrared observations challenges a previous groundbreaking claim. Three years ago, this galaxy made news for hosting an unusually massive and heavily dust-obscured black hole formed through direct collapse. Led by Fan Zou of the University of Michigan, the new study reports no signs of hidden black hole activity. The paper, published in The Astrophysical Journal on Oct. 14, suggests UHZ1 could be a low-mass, metal-poor, star-forming galaxy.

At the Sanaga-Yong sanctuary, which she founded in 1999, there are 75 chimpanzees to feed four times a day and monitor for physical or behavioural issues. Of those, more than 30 need to be given routine birth-control medications, four are babies requiring round-the-clock care, and two are rowdy teenagers currently being integrated into new social groups.

Space data centers could end stargazing as we know it
stories.summary: Sprawling networks of space data centers could make it nearly impossible for humans to stargaze. That's just one of the many risks that come with placing tens of thousands of AI computers into orbit, according to a new report. Why it matters: Most Americans don't want data centers built near them, but putting them in space brings a new set of problems. Threat level: "Companies and policymakers should proceed with great caution," top academic researchers warn in a report for the Innovation for Cool Earth Forum, an annual event hosted by the Japanese government. If space data centers proliferate, the "most visible points of light in the sky during much of the night in much of the world could be satellites, not stars," the report said, mirroring astronomers ' worries. If the U.S. military adopts the technology, the data centers could become potential targets during future space conflicts .
